Flash remediation — Phase 2a: the axial case, settled

The Phase 2 axial (detector-row truncation) story: geometry, the taper-vs-padding experiment, and its robustness riders · 2026-07-08 · overview and other pages: index.html · plan of record: flash_remediation_plan.md · Phase 1 characterization: phase_1_results.html · the radial case: phase_2b_radial_results.html · scripts: plans/experiments/flash_remediation/

TL;DR. For axial (row) truncation, the answer is: pad the recon in z by a geometry-derived scale, and do not taper. Padding beats the row taper at every level (0.141 vs 0.344 truncated-end NRMSE), adding a taper on top of padding makes things worse, and it turns out z-padding is bounded by pure geometry — no measured ray reaches |z| > (SID+R)/SID × the half-slab, confirmed bit-exactly — so "full" padding is always affordable. The row taper is retired for the axial case. A three-regime robustness rider (wider cone angle, BGA-style regularization, photon noise with transmission weights) preserved the ranking everywhere.

1  Where this page fits

Phase 1 established that both flash artifacts are model-support problems and that scale_recon_shape padding essentially eliminates them. Phase 2 asks the follow-up question: which remediation should actually ship, per axis, and with what parameters? Each sub-campaign gets its own page; this one is the axial (detector-row truncation) story: the geometry that frames it (§2), the taper-vs-padding experiment (§3), and the robustness riders (§4). The radial case lives in phase_2b_radial_results.html, the split_sino_recon seam study will follow, and index.html has the full map.

The machinery carries over from Phase 1: an enlarged ground-truth phantom projected through the real detector, iteration-by-iteration tracking, error split by region against the aligned truth crop, and visual quality as the deciding metric. One bookkeeping note: the laminate phase in the P2a phantom shifted relative to Phase 1 (the band pattern is computed on the larger ground-truth phantom), so don't compare P2a's absolute numbers to Phase 1's — every variant within P2a shares one phantom, which is the comparison that matters.

2  The geometry that frames the axial case

Notation. SID — source-to-iso (rotation axis) distance; SDD — source-to-detector distance (magnification = SDD/SID); C, δc — detector channel count and pitch, so (C/2)·δc is the detector half-width; hmax — the detector half-height ((rows/2)·δrow); R — the field-of-view radius at the axis. All in the model's physical (ALU) units.

Before any variant ran, the geometry handed us a structural result that shaped the whole sub-campaign. With the source in the iso plane (a circular orbit — the setting of all these cases), a ray to the top detector row climbs highest at the far edge of the FoV, reaching |z| = hmax·(SID+R)/SDD — that's (SID+R)/SID times the covered slab's half-height. The "covered slab" here is exactly mbirjax's default recon z-extent: auto_set_recon_geometry maps the detector height to the axis (half-height hmax·SID/SDD), so the default support's top and bottom touch the cone precisely at the rotation axis. Material beyond the visibility height never projects onto the detector at all, so "full" z-padding is bounded by pure geometry: a slice scale of at most 1 + R/SID plus a small PSF margin. And R itself comes from the fan: the detector half-width mapped back through the magnification. The two cartoons unpack those formulas and where the padding and taper quantities live in them.

Top view — the fan sets R

R is the detector half-width mapped back to the axis: R = (C/2)·δc·SID/SDD, by similar triangles on the fan rays. The only ratio the axial analysis needs is R/SID = C·δc/(2·SDD) — the fan half-angle, set by detector width and SDD alone. Magnification per se cancels (moving the object changes R and SID together), and detector rows never appear — which is why "more rows / bigger cone angle" changed nothing fractionally in P2a-R.

Side view — visibility, padding, and taper in z

In z, everything follows from the top ray. It crosses the axis at hmax·SID/SDD — the covered slab's half-height, which is exactly the default recon z-extent — and keeps climbing to hmax·(SID+R)/SDD at the far edge of the FoV. The red wedges between those two heights are visible but outside the default support: that is exactly what full padding (dashed red outline) must cover, and nothing above it ever projects — the padding bound. The dashed orange line is the threshold ray through the wedge's square corner (the slab's far top corner): detector rows beyond where it lands (fraction R/(SID+R) of the half-height, past the orange tick) have rays that exit the slab inside the FoV — the row-taper candidates, and also the reason the end wedge of half-sampled slices scales with R/SID.

P2a verified the bound the blunt way — extending the phantom far past the visibility height changed the sinogram by max |Δ| = exactly 0.0, bit for bit, at two different R/SID ratios (§3 and §4). Practical consequences: the "object too long to pad" scenario cannot exist in z; the right padding scale is computable rather than swept; and padding past the bound buys nothing.

3  P2a — axial truncation: taper vs padding

The setup is the Phase 1 SiC-like case: a laminated cylinder (radius 0.75× the FoV, so no lateral truncation) whose top extends past the covered slab, cone beam at magnification 2, 128 views, 40 iterations. On it we ran seven variants: padding at four levels {none, partial ×1.094, full ×1.188, overfull ×1.7} crossed with the row taper {off, on}, the taper being the quarter-sine ramp from the split_sino_recon precedent applied to the truncated side's edge rows. Taper widths come from the geometry — 6 rows on the default slab, 3 on the partially padded slab, and 0 on the fully padded slab (so the "full + taper" variant forces 6 rows, deliberately, to see what tapering costs when geometry says it isn't needed).

The geometry of §2 fixed the padding levels before anything ran: the visibility bound is 1.125 × the half-slab here, so "full" padding is scale 1.19 (bound + PSF margin), and the far-overshoot identity check came back max |Δ| = exactly 0.0, bit for bit — material past the bound truly never projects. The variants' job was then to verify that the bound is also the quality knee, and it is: overfull ties full to the third decimal.

What this settles

All three hypotheses got clean answers. Taper-alone blurs real end structure (H1): confirmed — it trades the ringing for the prior-extrapolation smear and stays 2.4× behind any padding. With full padding the taper is unnecessary (H2): confirmed, and then some — it isn't just unnecessary, it actively degrades the end (0.141 → 0.220). The combo wins at partial padding (H3): refuted — the taper hurts there too (0.154 → 0.215). The reason H3 fails is the geometry bound again: the visible-material band above the slab is thin (at most 12.5% of the half-slab here), so even "partial" padding covers most of it, leaving the taper nothing to fix and data to destroy.

One honest ceiling runs through all of it: every variant, full padding included, smooths the final laminate band in the top ~3 slices. Voxels at the top of the slab project past the detector edge for roughly half the views — the classic cone-beam end wedge — so those slices are half-sampled. That is missing data, not inconsistency; no weighting or padding can restore it, and it sets the quality floor any remediation should be judged against.

The P2a recommendation: for axial truncation, pad in z by the geometry-derived scale — (max_visible_z + PSF margin) / half-slab, available as cone_axial_geometry() in the experiment machinery — and do not taper. The row taper is retired for the axial case; the niche it was designed for (padding impractical) does not exist in z. For the split-seam study this tilts the prior toward the no-taper variant, but the split is a genuinely different situation (its extension gets data through overlap rows, and the prior-context requirement is central there), so P2c still gets its own measurement.

4  Does it survive other regimes? (P2a-R)

P2a ran at one geometry, default regularization, and no noise — so before building on the recommendation, we stress-tested the ranking {none, taper, pad_full} in three regimes chosen to probe where it could plausibly bend. The §2 geometry chose the first one: since every fractional quantity is governed by the lateral fan ratio R/SID alone, "higher magnification" and "more rows / bigger cone angle" collapse into a single axis — widen R/SID — realized as R1's wide-cone configuration (shorter SDD, doubled rows; the fan widens with it). The regularization and noise questions became R2 and R3, kept as independent single-variable probes — R2 changes the regularization with no noise, R3 adds noise at default regularization — since changing both at once would confound which one moved the result.

Regime (end NRMSE, iter 40)nonetaperpad_full
R1: wide cone (SDD 4C→2.5C, rows 64→128; R/SID 0.125→0.200) 1.0950.7180.253
R2: sharpness 2, snr_db 35 (the BGA regime) 0.7800.2990.150
R3: photon noise (i0 = 10⁴) + transmission weights, default regularization 0.6850.2550.075

The recommendation survives all three regimes, and interior NRMSE stayed variant-independent in every one. Two riders for the rest of the campaign: P2b should carry sharpness and noise configurations from the start — as separate probes, like R2/R3 here — since the radial case's global bias makes regime-dependence more plausible there than it was here; and expectations for SiC-like wide-cone scans should include the deeper sampling wedge at the ends — no remediation will recover that band.

5  Reproduction

P2a: plans/experiments/flash_remediation/z_taper_pad_grid.py (shared machinery in truncation_common.py: cone_axial_geometry, make_row_taper_weights, weights support in the tracked-recon loop). All knobs at the top, no CLI args; all seven variants take ~30 min on local CPU in the mbirjax conda env, and figures_only = True rebuilds these figures from saved results in about a minute. Figures land in figures/p2a_* and are embedded here (the repo gitignores PNGs); metrics and final volumes in results/p2a_*.
